title: The Bishop Pair
subtitle: Two bishops cover every square on the board — keep them.
goals: Open the position when you hold it
Decline trades that give it away

steps.say: One bishop sees half the board forever. TWO bishops see all of it — and that difference is worth roughly half a pawn in most positions, more as the board opens. Strong players treat the bishop pair as a real material advantage: they avoid trading either one, and they open lines to make them count. The corollary matters just as much: when your opponent has the pair, trade one off at the first chance.

steps.prompt: Your bishop is eyed by Black's knight and bishop. Keep it — and improve it!
hints: Every trade of a bishop hands away half of your future advantage. Find a square where the bishop is both safe and active.
Bc5 grabs an active diagonal, hits f8 and keeps the pair intact.

line.say: The bishop steps to an aggressive square and — crucially — stays on the board. Every exchange you decline here preserves an advantage that grows as pawns come off. 'Two bishops' is not a slogan; it's a half-pawn you can bank.

rejections.say: Also safe, but it invites ...Nxd4 and suddenly you're down to one bishop. Before every bishop move, ask: does this square offer a trade my opponent WANTS?
A fine-looking knight move that ignores the real asset. With two bishops your plan is to keep them and open lines — knight play comes second.

steps.wrongSay: Move the bishop somewhere active where it cannot be traded off.
steps.successSay: Keep the pair, open the board — the two halves of the same plan.

steps.prompt: You hold both bishops against bishop and knight. Play the move that makes them bite!
hints: Bishops love open diagonals. Which move puts a bishop on the long diagonal and eyes both wings?
Bd2–c3 style ideas are slow; here Bc5 grabs an open diagonal at once and keeps both bishops.

line.say: The bishops now rake diagonals across the whole board, and Black's knight has no protected square in front of them. This is the pair converting: not by tactics, but by controlling squares neither bishop could reach alone.

rejections.say: A pawn grab that walks into ...Ra8 trapping the bishop — and even if it escaped, you'd be trading your greatest asset for a wing pawn. With the pair, patience beats greed.

steps.wrongSay: Activate a bishop along a long diagonal without trading anything.
steps.successSay: Two bishops on open diagonals beat bishop-and-knight in almost every endgame.

steps.say: The practical rules: (1) With the pair, open the position and avoid trades. (2) Against the pair, trade one bishop even at the cost of a tempo, or keep the position closed so the bishops bump into pawns. (3) In endgames, two bishops beat bishop-and-knight so consistently that many strong players will decline a pawn to keep them.
